figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Illustration of MM-Grounding-DINO. Given image and text description, a text backbone and an image backbone are first utilized to extract text and image features respectively. The images and text features are then fed into the feature enhancer module to perform deep cross-modality fusion. After fusing, a language-guided query selection module is employed to extract cross-modality queries from the image features. These cross-modality queries are subsequently inputted into a cross-modality decoder, which is designed to probe the desired features from the two modal features. The output queries generated by the final layer of the decoder are then utilized for the prediction of object boxes and corresponding phrases

abstract: Grounding-DINO is a state-of-the-art open-set detection model that tackles multiple vision tasks including Open-Vocabulary Detection (OVD), Phrase Grounding (PG), and Referring Expression Comprehension (REC). Its effectiveness has led to its widespread adoption as a mainstream architecture for various downstream applications. However, despite its significance, the original Grounding-DINO model lacks comprehensive public technical details due to the unavailability of its training code. To bridge this gap, we present MM-Grounding-DINO, an open-source, comprehensive, and user-friendly pipeline, which is built with the MMDetection toolbox. It adopts abundant vision datasets for pre-training and various detection and grounding datasets for fine-tuning. We give a comprehensive analysis of each reported result and detailed settings for reproduction. The extensive experiments on the benchmarks mentioned demonstrate that our MM-Grounding-DINO-Tiny outperforms the Grounding-DINO-Tiny baseline. We release all our models to the research community. Codes and trained models are released at https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection/tree/main/configs/mm_grounding_dino.

sections.body: The paper rebuilds Grounding-DINO in MMDetection because the original release included only test and demo code. The structure is kept, with changes only at initialization. Pretraining adds COCO, Objects365, GRIT, V3Det, the RefCOCO family, and GQA with Flickr30k Entities. Cap4M is not open-source, so GRIT and V3Det substitute for it. Evaluation covers COCO, LVIS, RefCOCO/+/g, Flickr30k Entities, ODinW13/35, gRefCOCO and D3. The stated headline results are that MM-Grounding-DINO-Tiny reaches zero-shot 50.6 mAP on COCO and 41.4 mAP on LVIS mini, and surpasses Grounding-DINO-Tiny on REC. The authors claim to be the first to evaluate across this set of datasets.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Grounding-DINO's training code is unreleased, so the authors rebuild it in MMDetection and extend benchmarks for three grounding tasks.

sections.body: The model keeps the Grounding-DINO design: a BERT-based uncased text encoder, a Swin Transformer image backbone, a feature enhancer, a language-guided query selection module with `num_query` set to 900, and a cross-modality decoder. Boxes are trained with L1 and GIoU losses, and classification uses a focal loss as a contrastive loss between boxes and language tokens. The main change is a bias added when initializing the contrastive embedding, which the authors say reduces the initial loss and speeds convergence. Training uses 15 datasets in three groups. GRIT is sampled at 500,000 images per epoch. MM-G-Tiny trained on 32 NVIDIA 3090 GPUs with batch size 128 for 30 epochs. MM-G-Large was still training.
sections.heading: Approach
sections.headline: Grounding-DINO's cross-modality architecture is kept, with a bias added to the contrastive embedding and random negative samples in augmentation.

sections.body: MM-G-T(c1) reaches 50.5 mAP on COCO against 48.4 for G-DINO-T(c), and MM-G-T(a), trained on Objects365 only, reaches 48.5. On LVIS MiniVal, MM-G-T(c3) reaches 41.4 mAP and the text reports a gain of +12.6 AP over G-DINO-T(c). On RefCOCO/+/g, MM-G-T(c3) is above G-DINO-T(c) on every split. The authors note that adding V3Det does not help COCO zero-shot results and may hurt them, and that RefCOCO/+/g may be overly simple. With fine-tuning, the model reaches 69.1 AP on the haze dataset after 12 epochs and gains 35.7 mAP on the underwater RUOD dataset after 12 epochs. On Cityscapes it gains 17.3 mAP after 50 epochs. On the brain tumor dataset it underperforms Cascade-DINO.
sections.heading: Main Results
sections.headline: Zero-shot tests show the Tiny variants beat Grounding-DINO-Tiny on detection and referring-expression benchmarks, with the largest gains on the long-tail benchmark.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the contributions: MM-Grounding-DINO is an open-sourced grounding baseline pretrained on abundant vision datasets, covering OVD, PG and REC. The authors say all available benchmarks for these tasks are extended and that all evaluation metrics are available in MMDetection. They state that the model outperforms, or is on par with, the Grounding-DINO baseline across the benchmarks mentioned. The section gives no new numbers and states no limitations; those appear in Section 3 and the Appendix.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: The authors conclude the open pipeline matches or beats the Grounding-DINO baseline and release it as a shared resource.

sections.body: Table 12 varies the gRefCOCO threshold: 0.8 gives the highest F1 on the validation set, while 0.5 works better on testA and testB. Table 13 shows MM-G-T(c) below G-DINO-T on Flickr30K Entities, and the authors note this is not zero-shot because GoldG includes Flickr30K images. Table 14 gives per-dataset ODinW results. Table 15 shows that fine-tuning only on base categories raises novel-category mAP by +1.5. The visualizations show noisy pretraining captions and GRIT pseudo-label errors. The model tends to prioritize nouns, ignores the word 'without', and performs suboptimally on position descriptions.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix adds threshold sweeps, per-dataset tables for three benchmarks, open-vocabulary fine-tuning results and failure-case visualizations.
